_purpose: The vocabulary of what mcgyvr can be asked to do. Each entry states what accepting it promises (`guarantee`), which family of the ladder it may start on (`starts_on`), which use case it belongs to (`use_case`), and what evidence a contract of that type must carry (`required_evidence`). This file is the only definition: adding a task type is an edit here, not a code change. See data/README.md for how the vocabulary was validated and what was removed from it.

vendored_from._note: The starting vocabulary was inherited from local-ai's triage map. It was inherited, not validated. `excluded` below records what did not survive validation and why.

families.name: deterministic
families.doc: Tools. A program executes the change; no model is asked and no tokens are spent. Exactly one attempt, because a tool fails identically on retry.

families.name: local
families.doc: Models served by a source needing no credential. The keyless install runs here with the deterministic gate as its whole acceptance bar.

families.name: api
families.doc: Models served by a source needing a credential. The dearest family, and the one the north star measures spend against.

_families_note: Ordered cheapest to dearest. A family is the ladder-independent way to say where work starts: rung names are chosen by whoever wrote the config, so a catalog that named rungs would only be valid on the machine it was written for. A family resolves against any ladder — a rung is `api` when its unit declares an `api_key_env` and `local` when it does not.

use_cases.name: coding
use_cases.doc: Scoped edits to a repository, judged by a deterministic gate over code.

use_cases.name: chat
use_cases.doc: Raw prompt-to-response over a bound fleet; no gate, an endpoint for a harness.

use_cases.name: agent
use_cases.doc: Gated personal-assistant tasks, judged by grounded citations plus safety over plain prose; the backend is llama.cpp / vLLM with tool-calling, a serving-layer capability rather than a gate rung.

use_cases.name: media-gen
use_cases.doc: Image, video and speech generation, judged by media-valid, safety and ASR gates.

evidence_kinds.name: gate
evidence_kinds.doc: The deterministic acceptance gate. The floor under every coding type; chat is ungated, and agent and media-gen are judged by their own structural evidence through the gate's output-checks rung.

evidence_kinds.name: tool_idempotent
evidence_kinds.doc: Re-running the tool that produced the change produces no further change. Available only to the deterministic family, where a tool owns the output.

evidence_kinds.name: references_resolved
evidence_kinds.doc: Every reference the index resolved was updated. What the index could not resolve — dynamic access, reflection, strings — is reported as unhandled rather than assumed absent.

evidence_kinds.name: no_semantic_change
evidence_kinds.doc: The parsed structure is unchanged apart from the region the type is allowed to touch. A structural check, so the gate can judge it without running anything.

evidence_kinds.name: type_check
evidence_kinds.doc: The project's type checker passes on the changed target.

evidence_kinds.name: tests_pass
evidence_kinds.doc: The contract's acceptance commands pass in the sandbox.

evidence_kinds.name: failing_test_first
evidence_kinds.doc: An acceptance command that demonstrates the defect — it must fail before the change and pass after. Without it a fix is indistinguishable from a plausible edit. Carried in the contract's `demonstration` list, not `acceptance`: the two lists have opposite baseline expectations, and one flat list cannot say which command is which (#183).

evidence_kinds.name: media_valid
evidence_kinds.doc: The output artifact is a valid file of the declared media kind — correct format, dimensions or duration. A structural check the gate makes itself, so it needs no contract command.

evidence_kinds.name: safety_pass
evidence_kinds.doc: A deterministic safety classifier passes on the output. One kind serves media and text outputs alike — the gate runs it, the contract does not.

evidence_kinds.name: asr_wer
evidence_kinds.doc: An ASR pass transcribes the audio output and its word-error-rate against the transcript stays under the contract's threshold. The transcript is the contract's own target, so the gate judges it without a human.

evidence_kinds.name: grounded
evidence_kinds.doc: Every claim the reply makes cites a source the contract provided, so nothing is asserted that the corpus did not carry. A structural check, not a judgement.

_evidence_note: `baseline` states what the evidence's commands must do on the unchanged tree — `pass` for a regression signal, `fail` for a demonstration — and is only meaningful where `needs_commands` is true. It is data here rather than a rule in code so that the contract loader can check each command-needing kind against the right contract list (`acceptance` for pass, `demonstration` for fail) without naming any evidence kind (#183).

task_types.name: format
task_types.guarantee: The target is byte-identical to what the project's own formatter produces. No semantic change, and nothing is decided that the formatter's configuration did not already decide.
task_types.warrant: structural — the project's formatter is the definition of the correct output, so there is nothing for a model to be better at.
task_types.doc: Reformat existing code with the project's own formatter.

task_types.name: import_sort
task_types.guarantee: Imports are ordered as the project's own tool orders them, with no other change to the file.
task_types.warrant: structural — same argument as `format`; the tool's configuration is the specification.
task_types.doc: Order imports with the project's own tool.

task_types.name: lint_fix
task_types.guarantee: Every autofix the project's linter applies is applied, and nothing else is. A diagnostic the linter will not fix itself is explicitly out of scope for this type rather than handed to a model under the same name.
task_types.warrant: structural — the linter decides both what is wrong and what the fix is.
task_types.doc: Apply the project linter's own autofixes.

task_types.name: rename_symbol
task_types.guarantee: Every reference the index resolved is renamed, across every file that holds one. References the index could not resolve are reported, not silently left behind.
task_types.warrant: structural — the index (#47) already resolved the references, so this fans across files without a model. It is the only multi-file type in the catalog, and it is deterministic for exactly that reason.
task_types.doc: Rename a symbol across the files that reference it.

task_types.name: code
task_types.guarantee: A scoped change to one target, judged by the deterministic gate. Which checks back the judgement is derived from the contract itself: a `demonstration` adds `failing_test_first`, an `acceptance` adds `tests_pass`, `no_semantic_change: true` adds `no_semantic_change`, and `type_check: true` adds `type_check`; the gate is always the floor.
task_types.warrant: One type for every local coding task. The five types this collapses (`docstring`, `type_annotation`, `function_implementation`, `test_scaffold`, `bug_fix`) differed only in which evidence bundle the contract had to carry, and the model was asked to choose among near-duplicates — a mechanism (type + command) leaking into the model's relevance authority. The model now states relevance and the orthogonal flags; the evidence is derived, not chosen.
task_types.doc: Make a scoped edit to one named target. The gate judges the change, and the contract's own fields decide which checks back the judgement.

task_types.name: chat
task_types.guarantee: The reply is the answer. Nothing judges it — chat is a raw prompt-to-response endpoint, and whether the answer is right is the harness's question, not the gate's.
task_types.warrant: There is no bar to clear — chat is a raw endpoint, so nothing is spent judging and the reply is served straight back.
task_types.doc: Answer a prompt directly, ungated. The raw endpoint of the chat use case.

task_types.name: agent
task_types.guarantee: The reply cites the contract's sources and clears the safety classifier, as plain prose — every claim is grounded, nothing unsafe is served, and the reply is raw text, not a file.
task_types.warrant: structural — grounded and safety_pass are checks the gate makes itself, and the prose output protocol is the reply's format, so a wrong, unsafe or malformed answer is caught without a contract command.
task_types.doc: Answer a prompt with a grounded, safe reply in plain prose, judged by the gate's output checks.

excluded.name: comment_addition
excluded.reason: No acceptance evidence distinguishes a good comment from a bad one, or from no change at all. Where the comment is a docstring the gate can at least assert nothing else moved — that shape is now `code` with `no_semantic_change: true`; a bare comment leaves the gate with nothing to judge.

excluded.name: string_literal_edit
excluded.reason: An exact edit at a known location is an operation the deterministic tier should perform outright, not a kind of work to route; as a task type it would spend a model rung on something no model is needed for.

excluded.name: config_edit
excluded.reason: The gate's structural checks are Python and JS/TS only. A YAML or TOML change has no adapter, so acceptance would rest on nothing but the file still parsing — too thin a bar for a file that decides how everything else runs. Revisit when an adapter covers the format.

excluded.name: multi_file_refactor
excluded.reason: Structurally unservable, not merely hard: the worker output protocol is one file's complete content in one fenced block (#25), so no model rung can emit a coordinated multi-file change at all. Routing it optimistically would guarantee a failure at the parse step rather than at the gate. `rename_symbol` is the one multi-file operation the catalog carries, and it is deterministic precisely because the index resolves the references instead of a model guessing them.

excluded.name: algorithm_implementation
excluded.reason: Not a distinct guarantee. The contract already carries the interface and the acceptance commands, so this differs from a `code` contract that states both only in how hard the prompt is — and difficulty is what the ladder escalates over, not a name in the vocabulary.

excluded.name: simple_bug_fix
excluded.reason: Encodes difficulty in the type name. Difficulty is already routing state, resolved by escalation; a second copy in the vocabulary is a copy that can disagree with the first.

excluded.name: complex_bug_fix
excluded.reason: Same as `simple_bug_fix` — difficulty is not a type.

excluded.name: docstring
excluded.reason: Folded into `code`. A docstring change is `code` with `no_semantic_change: true` — the gate compares the parsed structure and rejects an edit that changed code while claiming only to document it.

excluded.name: type_annotation
excluded.reason: Folded into `code`. Annotation is `code` with `no_semantic_change: true` and `type_check: true` — the project's own type checker is the judge of whether the inference was right.

excluded.name: function_implementation
excluded.reason: Folded into `code`. Implementing one function against a stated interface is `code` with `interface` and an `acceptance` command.

excluded.name: test_scaffold
excluded.reason: Folded into `code`. Writing tests for one named target is `code` whose `target` is the test file, so the scope stays inverted and a worker cannot make a test pass by changing what it tests.

excluded.name: bug_fix
excluded.reason: Folded into `code`. A fix is `code` with a `demonstration` that fails before the change and passes after, plus an optional `acceptance` suite.

excluded.name: interface_design
excluded.reason: No acceptance evidence exists for it. A designed interface has no command that can fail, so the deterministic gate cannot accept it and a model verifier would be the only judge — which spends expensive tokens to decide whether expensive tokens were well spent, and inverts the north star. Design is the calling agent's work; mcgyvr owns what is below the contract.
